elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, any drug, a vapor releasing substance, or combination thereof
If impaired to the slightest degree, or with BAC .08+ (or .04+ commercial vehicle)
mandatory_minimum: 24 consecutive hours in jail (first offense); 30 days (second); 10 days served (first, with 9 suspended)
enhancements: BAC .15+ — Extreme DUI (§ 28-1382, enhanced mandatory minimums)
BAC .20+ — Super Extreme DUI (§ 28-1382(A)(2), further enhanced)
Aggravated DUI (§ 28-1383): suspended/revoked license, third within 84 months, wrong-way driving, child under 15 in vehicle
notes: Arizona is known for very strict DUI enforcement. Mandatory jail time even for first offense. Extreme DUI (.15+) has 30-day minimum jail. Super Extreme (.20+) has 45-day minimum.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While impaired to the slightest degree by alcohol or drugs
Or with BAC .08 or higher
No prior DUI convictions within 84 months
mandatory_minimum: 10 days jail (9 may be suspended with completion of screening); $1,250 fine plus surcharges
enhancements: BAC .15+ (Extreme DUI — mandatory 30 consecutive days jail)
BAC .20+ (Super Extreme DUI — mandatory 45 consecutive days jail)
Child under 15 in vehicle (aggravated, Class 6 Felony)
notes: Mandatory ignition interlock device for 12 months. License suspension 90 days. Alcohol screening and education required.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (second within 84 months); Class 4 Felony (third within 84 months — aggravated)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle while impaired or with BAC .08+
One or more prior DUI convictions within 84 months (7 years)
mandatory_minimum: 90 days jail with 60 suspended (second); 4 months prison (aggravated third)
enhancements: Third offense within 84 months (aggravated, Class 4 Felony)
Driving on suspended/revoked license at time of DUI
notes: 84-month (7-year) lookback period. Third offense within lookback is aggravated DUI — a Class 4 Felony with mandatory prison time. License revocation 1 year for second offense.

penalty_min: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of any drug defined in § 13-3401
Or while there is any drug or its metabolite in the defendant's body
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Metabolite of Schedule I substance in body (per se violation under § 28-1381(A)(3))
notes: Arizona has a per se drug DUI law — any detectable amount of a drug or its metabolite in the body while driving is a violation. Medical marijuana is an affirmative defense if not impaired (Dobson v. McClennen).

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In reckless disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: 8 points on driving record. Common plea-down from DUI. License suspension 90 days for excessive speed reckless driving.

statute_title: Duty to Stop — Accident Involving Injury or Death
offense_class: Class 3 Felony (death); Class 5 Felony (serious injury); Class 2 Misdemeanor (injury, § 28-662); Class 3 Misdemeanor (property, § 28-663)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene
Defendant failed to render reasonable assistance or provide identification
notes: Leaving the scene of a fatal accident is a Class 3 Felony in Arizona. Property damage only is a Class 3 Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Arizona does not have a separate vehicular homicide statute. DUI deaths are typically charged as manslaughter (Class 2 Felony) or second-degree murder (depraved heart).

elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Charged under the general manslaughter statute. Negligent homicide (§ 13-1102, Class 4 Felony) available for criminal negligence deaths.

statute_title: Driving on a Suspended, Revoked, or Canceled License
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a highway
While defendant's license was suspended, canceled, revoked, or refused
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
enhancements: Driving on DUI-suspended license (aggravated DUI, Class 4 Felony under § 28-1383)
notes: Driving on a DUI-related suspension is an aggravated DUI — a Class 4 Felony. Other suspended license driving is a Class 1 Misdemeanor.

statute_title: Unlawful Flight from Pursuing Law Enforcement Vehicle
elements: A law enforcement vehicle with activated emergency lights or siren pursued the defendant
Defendant willfully fled or attempted to elude the pursuing vehicle
enhancements: Causing death or serious injury during flight
notes: Class 5 Felony regardless of whether anyone is injured. Additional charges possible if others are endangered during the pursuit.

statute_title: Possession of a Dangerous Drug / Drug Offense
offense_class: Class 4 Felony (dangerous drugs); Class 6 Felony (other substances)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a dangerous drug or narcotic drug
Without a valid prescription or lawful authority
notes: Prop 200 (1996) requires probation, not prison, for first and second possession offenses. Prop 207 (2020) legalized recreational marijuana for 21+. Possession of other drugs remains criminal.

statute_title: Personal Possession and Use of Marijuana
offense_class: Legal for 21+ (1 oz or less); Petty offense (2.5 oz or less over 1 oz); Class 6 Felony (over 2.5 oz); Class 5 Felony (over threshold for sale)
elements: For criminal charge: defendant possessed marijuana in excess of legal limits
Or defendant was under 21 and possessed marijuana
notes: Prop 207 (2020) legalized recreational marijuana. Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz (5g concentrate). Over 2.5 oz becomes a felony. Under 21 possession is a petty offense.

statute_title: Possession of a Dangerous Drug — Cocaine
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is classified as a dangerous drug under A.R.S. § 13-3401
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Threshold amount (9 grams — triggers mandatory prison under § 13-3408(B))
notes: Prop 200 mandates probation for first two simple possession convictions. Possession of threshold amount (9g cocaine) triggers mandatory prison.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine falls under the 'narcotic drugs' category in Arizona. Threshold amount is 9 grams for mandatory prison.

statute_title: Transportation of Dangerous Drugs / Narcotics for Sale
elements: Defendant transported, imported, or offered to transport
A dangerous drug or narcotic drug into Arizona
For sale
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory prison (no probation) for threshold amounts
notes: Threshold amounts: meth 9g, cocaine 9g, heroin 1g, LSD 0.5ml, marijuana 2 lbs. Over threshold = mandatory prison, no probation. Class 2 Felony.

statute_title: Possession of Dangerous Drug for Sale
elements: Defendant possessed a dangerous drug
For the purpose of sale
notes: Possession for sale is the same class as actual sale. Intent to sell inferred from quantity, packaging, and circumstances.

elements: Defendant manufactured a dangerous drug
Or possessed equipment or chemicals with intent to manufacture
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries additional penalties. Cleanup costs assessed as restitution.

offense_class: Class 6 Felony (possession); Class 6 Felony (use/possession with intent to use)
elements: Defendant used or possessed with intent to use drug paraphernalia

To plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, process, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale, or otherwise introduce into the human body a drug
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor
notes: Marijuana paraphernalia is legal for adults 21+ under Prop 207. Paraphernalia for other drugs remains a Class 6 Felony. Prop 200 mandates probation for first two drug possession offenses.

statute_title: Possession of Narcotic/Dangerous Drug for Sale
elements: Defendant possessed a narcotic or dangerous drug
With intent to sell or distribute
Without lawful authority
notes: Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, and cash. Threshold amounts trigger mandatory prison sentences.

penalty_min: Life with possibility of release after 25 years (non-capital)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With premeditation
Or the death occurred during the commission of specified felonies (felony murder)
Or defendant intentionally killed a law enforcement officer in the line of duty
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment (natural life or 25 years to life)
notes: Arizona is a death penalty state. Natural life means no possibility of release. Felony murder applies during enumerated felonies. Death sentence requires unanimous jury finding of aggravating factors.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused the death of another person without premeditation
Or caused the death by conduct showing extreme indifference to human life
Or caused the death while intentionally committing the act causing death knowing it would cause death
notes: Covers intentional killing without premeditation and depraved-heart/extreme indifference murder. Presumptive sentence is 10 years for first offense.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
The killing was committed upon a sudden quarrel or heat of passion
Resulting from adequate provocation by the victim
notes: Arizona's manslaughter statute (§ 13-1103) covers both heat-of-passion (what other states call voluntary manslaughter) and reckless killing.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
notes: Arizona uses 'negligent homicide' (§ 13-1102) for what most states call involuntary manslaughter. Criminal negligence standard: failure to perceive a substantial and unjustifiable risk.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (serious physical injury); Class 3 Felony (deadly weapon/dangerous instrument); Class 5-6 Felony (other aggravating factors)
elements: Defendant committed assault as defined in § 13-1203
Plus an aggravating factor: causing serious physical injury, using a deadly weapon, victim is bound/restrained, victim is under 15, assault on officer/teacher/healthcare worker, etc.
mandatory_minimum: 5 years (if dangerous offense with deadly weapon/dangerous instrument)
notes: Arizona has 13 ways to elevate simple assault to aggravated. 'Dangerous offense' designation (involving deadly weapon or causing serious injury) triggers mandatory prison time.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (physical injury); Class 2 Misdemeanor (reasonable apprehension); Class 3 Misdemeanor (touching to insult/provoke)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused physical injury to another (Class 1)
Or intentionally placed another in reasonable apprehension of imminent physical injury (Class 2)
Or knowingly touched another with intent to injure, insult, or provoke (Class 3)
notes: Three classes based on the type of assault. Physical injury = Class 1, threat = Class 2, offensive touching = Class 3.

elements: Defendant, in the course of taking any property of another from their person or immediate presence
Threatened or used force against any person with intent to coerce surrender of property or prevent resistance
notes: Base robbery is a Class 4 Felony. Aggravated robbery (§ 13-1903) with an accomplice is Class 3. Armed robbery (§ 13-1904) is Class 2.

elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon or simulated deadly weapon
Or used or threatened to use a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Dangerous offense designation makes prison mandatory. Presumptive term 7 years for first offense. Prior felonies dramatically increase the range.

penalty_max: 21 years (aggravated, first offense); natural life (if victim under 15 and sexual motivation)
elements: Defendant knowingly restrained another person
With intent to hold for ransom, as a shield or hostage, aid in commission of a felony, inflict injury, place in involuntary servitude, or sexual offense
notes: Always a dangerous offense when victim is restrained. If victim is released unharmed, may be mitigated. Kidnapping of a child under 15 with sexual motivation can result in natural life.

elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully damaged a structure or property
By knowingly causing a fire or explosion
enhancements: Arson of an occupied structure is a dangerous offense
notes: Three arson statutes: property (§ 13-1703, Class 4), structure (§ 13-1704, Class 4), occupied structure (§ 13-1705, Class 3). Occupied structure arson is a dangerous offense with mandatory prison.

elements: Defendant intended to commit first degree murder
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of the offense
notes: Attempt reduces the classification by one level (Class 1 → Class 2). Always a dangerous offense. Presumptive sentencing applies.

elements: Defendant committed assault
Using a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Dangerous offense designation makes prison mandatory. No probation available. Presumptive sentence is 5 years for first offense.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony ($25,000+); Class 3 Felony ($4,000-$25,000); Class 4 Felony ($3,000-$4,000); Class 5 Felony ($2,000-$3,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,000); Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly took control of property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner of the property
Without lawful authority or the owner's consent
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (Class 6 Felony minimum)
notes: Arizona has detailed value thresholds determining felony class. Theft of a firearm is always at least a Class 6 Felony regardless of value. Shoplifting has a separate statute (§ 13-1805).

elements: Defendant knowingly took control of property of another
Value exceeds $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Arizona does not use 'grand theft' terminology. The felony class is determined by value thresholds.

elements: Defendant knowingly took control of property of another
Value is less than $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Under $1,000 is a Class 1 Misdemeanor. Prior theft convictions may elevate classification.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,000); Class 5 Felony ($2,000+); Class 4 Felony (organized retail theft or third offense)
elements: Defendant knowingly concealed, took possession of, or charged less than the purchase price of goods
With intent to deprive the merchant of the goods
enhancements: Third shoplifting offense within 5 years (Class 4 Felony)
Use of device to defeat anti-theft measures
notes: Arizona has a specific shoplifting statute separate from general theft. Third offense within 5 years is automatic Class 4 Felony.

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a residential structure
With intent to commit any theft or any felony therein
enhancements: Possession of a deadly weapon during burglary
notes: Three degrees: first (§ 13-1508, armed in residential, Class 2), second (§ 13-1507, residential, Class 3), third (§ 13-1506, non-residential, Class 4).

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a residential structure
With intent to commit a theft or felony
enhancements: Armed during burglary (elevates to first degree, Class 2 Felony)
notes: Residential structure includes houses, apartments, and fenced residential yards. First-degree burglary (§ 13-1508) involves possession of a weapon, explosive, or dangerous instrument.

elements: Defendant knowingly took control of the means of transportation of another
Without lawful authority
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Arizona has a separate motor vehicle theft statute (§ 13-1814). Always a Class 3 Felony regardless of vehicle value.

offense_class: Same as theft classification by value
elements: Defendant knowingly received property that was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
Defendant knew or had reason to know the property was stolen
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Classification follows the same value thresholds as other theft.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony ($10,000+); Class 5 Felony ($2,000-$10,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,000); Class 1 Misdemeanor ($250-$1,000); Class 2 Misdemeanor (under $250)
elements: Defendant recklessly damaged or defaced property of another
Without the consent of the owner
notes: Arizona uses 'criminal damage' rather than vandalism. Detailed value thresholds determine the classification.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (third degree); Class 2 Misdemeanor (second degree); Class 1 Misdemeanor (first degree, residential)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully on property
After a reasonable request to leave, or where posted, or fenced
notes: Three degrees: first (§ 13-1504, residential, Class 1 Misdemeanor), second (§ 13-1503, non-residential structure, Class 2), third (§ 13-1502, land/real property, Class 3).

offense_class: Varies by value — Class 4 Felony ($10,000+) through Class 2 Misdemeanor (under $250)
elements: Defendant recklessly defaced, damaged, or tampered with property of another
Without consent of the owner
notes: Arizona uses 'criminal damage' as the equivalent of criminal mischief. Value thresholds determine the offense class.

offense_class: Varies by underlying offense — misdemeanor to felony
elements: Defendant committed a predicate offense (assault, criminal damage, disorderly conduct, etc.)
Against a spouse, former spouse, cohabitant, person with a child in common, romantic/sexual partner, or related by blood/court order
mandatory_minimum: Domestic violence offender treatment program required; 24-hour hold after arrest if against spouse/cohabitant
enhancements: Third DV offense within 84 months (aggravated DV, Class 5 Felony under § 13-3601.02)
Violation of order of protection (separate offense)
notes: Domestic violence is a designation in Arizona, not a standalone crime. It attaches to about 20 predicate offenses. Third conviction within 84 months is aggravated DV — a Class 5 Felony.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (with DV designation); Class 5 Felony (third within 84 months)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused physical injury
To a person in a domestic relationship
notes: Arizona does not have a separate battery statute. Assault with DV designation covers domestic battery situations.

statute_title: Child or Vulnerable Adult Abuse — Circumstances Likely to Produce Physical Injury
offense_class: Class 6 Felony (reckless/negligent endangerment); Class 5 Felony (knowingly/intentionally); Class 2 Felony (serious injury)
elements: Defendant, under circumstances likely to produce death or serious physical injury
Caused or permitted a child or vulnerable adult to suffer physical injury or be placed in a situation of unreasonable risk
enhancements: Death results (Class 2 Felony with dangerous designation)
notes: Arizona's child abuse statute (§ 13-3623) covers a broad range from negligent endangerment to intentional serious harm. Mental state determines the class.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (serious injury); Class 4 Felony (physical injury); Class 5 Felony (without injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused physical injury to a child
Under circumstances likely to produce death or serious physical injury
enhancements: Serious physical injury (Class 2 Felony, dangerous offense)
notes: Intentional or knowing child abuse with serious injury is a Class 2 Dangerous Felony — mandatory prison. CPS investigation triggered by any charge.

statute_title: Interfering with Judicial Proceedings — Violation of Order of Protection
offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first); Class 6 Felony (second within 12 months or involving threats/injury); Class 4 Felony (third within 24 months)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant knowingly violated the order
enhancements: Violation involving threats or physical injury
notes: Increasingly severe penalties for repeat violations. Violation while possessing a firearm is an additional offense.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in a course of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of their immediate family
Or would cause a reasonable person to fear death or that of an immediate family member
enhancements: Violation of protective order while stalking
notes: Stalking is always a felony in Arizona. 'Course of conduct' means two or more acts directed at, but not necessarily in the presence of, the person.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 6 Felony (against public officer or if prior DV harassment conviction)
elements: Defendant with intent to harass or with knowledge that the conduct was harassing
Anonymously or otherwise contacted, communicated, or made a credible threat to another person
Or followed another person in a public place
enhancements: Against a public officer or employee (Class 6 Felony under § 13-2921.01)
With DV designation and prior DV conviction
notes: Harassment with DV designation becomes part of the DV count for aggravated DV purposes.

offense_class: Same as child abuse classifications by mental state and injury
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult
Under circumstances likely to produce death or serious physical injury
notes: Vulnerable adults are protected under the same statute as children (§ 13-3623). Financial exploitation charged as theft. Mandatory reporting under § 46-454.

offense_class: Class 6 Felony (most violations); Class 4 Felony (some aggravated violations)
elements: Defendant possessed a deadly weapon or prohibited weapon
In a prohibited location or in a prohibited manner
notes: Arizona is a constitutional carry state — no permit needed for concealed carry by those legally allowed to possess firearms. Restrictions focus on prohibited persons and locations.

statute_title: Possession of a Deadly Weapon by Prohibited Possessor
elements: Defendant possessed a deadly weapon
Defendant was a prohibited possessor as defined in § 13-3101
Prohibited persons include those convicted of a felony, undocumented persons, and those found mentally incompetent
notes: Prohibited possessor defined in § 13-3101(A)(7). Includes felony convictions, domestic violence convictions, and those adjudicated mentally incompetent.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon in a Prohibited Location
elements: Defendant carried a deadly weapon
Into a prohibited location (polling place, school, government building, nuclear/hydroelectric facility, bar while consuming alcohol)
notes: Arizona adopted constitutional carry in 2010. No permit needed. Violations relate only to prohibited locations and prohibited persons.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
Within or into the limits of any municipality
With criminal negligence
enhancements: Discharge at an occupied structure or vehicle (§ 13-1211, Class 2 Felony)
notes: Shannon's Law (§ 13-3107) makes random gunfire within city limits a felony. Intentional discharge at an occupied structure is a Class 2 Felony under § 13-1211.

statute_title: Taking the Identity of Another Person or Entity
elements: Defendant knowingly took, purchased, manufactured, or recorded another person's personal identifying information
Without consent
With intent to obtain or use the information unlawfully
enhancements: Five or more victims (Class 3 Felony under § 13-2009)
notes: Aggravated identity theft (§ 13-2009, Class 3 Felony) applies when five or more victims or if the defendant is not a U.S. citizen. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Defendant, having control of property of another entrusted to defendant
Knowingly converted the property to defendant's own use or benefit
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute as conversion of entrusted property.

elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With intent to defraud
Or knowingly possessed a forged instrument
notes: Covers all types of forged documents. Possession of a forged instrument with intent to use is included.

elements: Defendant issued a check knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Defendant must be given 12 days' notice of dishonor before prosecution.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained any benefit by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, promises, or material omissions
Or defendant knowingly devised a scheme to defraud
enhancements: Scheme targeting elderly or vulnerable adults
notes: Arizona's fraud statute is broad. Class 2 Felony regardless of amount — making it one of the harshest in the nation. Separate computer fraud statute (§ 13-2316).

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Class 5 Felony (any amount); Class 6 Felony (possession of blank cards)
elements: Defendant used a credit card knowing it to be stolen, forged, canceled, or revoked
With intent to defraud
To obtain property or services
notes: Fraudulent credit card use is always a felony in Arizona regardless of amount.

elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Knowing or having reason to know the property involved was proceeds of an offense
With intent to promote the carrying on of unlawful activity or to conceal the source
notes: First degree: knowing the property is proceeds and conducting transaction to promote unlawful activity. Second degree: reason to know.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (dangerous crime against children if victim under 15)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in sexual intercourse or oral sexual contact
With any person without consent of that person
enhancements: Victim under 15 (dangerous crime against children — flat 13 years to natural life)
notes: Arizona uses 'sexual assault' for what most states call rape. Dangerous crime against children designation when victim is under 15 triggers extremely severe mandatory sentences.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in sexual intercourse or oral sexual contact
Without the consent of the other person
notes: Arizona does not have a separate 'rape' statute — sexual assault (§ 13-1406) covers all non-consensual sexual intercourse. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (adult victim); Class 6 Felony (victim under 15)
elements: Defendant exposed genitals or anus or the areola or nipple of the female breast
And another person was present
Defendant was reckless about whether the other person would be alarmed or offended
enhancements: Prior sex offense convictions (may trigger sex offender registration)
notes: Exposure to a minor under 15 is a Class 6 Felony. Two or more convictions require sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to engage in sexual conduct with another person
For a fee
Or solicited another to engage in such conduct
notes: Arizona has mandatory minimum jail time for prostitution-related offenses. Soliciting a minor is a serious felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly distributing, transporting, exhibiting, receiving, selling, purchasing, electronically transmitting, possessing, or exchanging any visual depiction
In which a minor is engaged in exploitive exhibition or sexual conduct
mandatory_minimum: 10 years per image (DCAC mandatory sentence for each count, must run consecutively)
notes: Arizona has among the harshest child exploitation penalties in the nation. Each image can be a separate count. Sentences must run consecutively. DCAC = dangerous crime against children.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration as required
notes: Must register within 10 days of release or change of address. Community notification applies. Level assignment determines notification scope.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (victim under 15 — DCAC); Class 6 Felony (victim 15-17)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in sexual intercourse or oral sexual contact
With a person under 18 years of age
mandatory_minimum: Flat 13 years (victim under 15, DCAC); no mandatory minimum (victim 15-17 if defendant is 19-)
enhancements: Victim under 15 (DCAC — mandatory prison, no probation, no pardon, no commutation)
notes: Age of consent is 18 in Arizona. For victims 15-17, defense of close in age (no more than 24 months difference or defendant is still in high school). Victim under 15 = DCAC with mandatory flat time.

elements: Defendant with intent to disturb the peace or quiet of a neighborhood, family, or person
Engaged in fighting, violent, or seriously disruptive behavior
Or made unreasonable noise, or used abusive or offensive language or gestures
notes: Disorderly conduct involving display or discharge of a deadly weapon is a Class 6 Felony. Otherwise Class 1 Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a person reasonably known to be a peace officer
From effecting an arrest
By using or threatening to use physical force, or by creating a substantial risk of causing physical injury
notes: Resisting arrest is always a felony in Arizona. Passive resistance without force is not covered by this statute.

elements: Defendant knowingly attempted to obstruct, delay, or prevent
The communication of information or testimony
To a peace officer, prosecutor, or other official conducting a criminal investigation
notes: Separate from hindering prosecution (§ 13-2510) and tampering with evidence (§ 13-2809).

offense_class: Varies (direct or indirect; civil or criminal)
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disorderly or disruptive behavior in the courtroom
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive. Arizona statute provides for both direct (in court) and indirect (outside court) contempt.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (felony case); Class 1 Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant was released on own recognizance or bail
Defendant knowingly failed to appear as required
notes: First degree (felony case) is Class 5 Felony. Second degree (misdemeanor case, § 13-2506) is Class 1 Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant initiated a false report to a law enforcement agency
Claiming that a felony or misdemeanor had occurred
Knowing the report was false
notes: Separate from false reporting of a bomb threat or emergency, which carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 6 Felony (to promote criminal street gang)
elements: Defendant threatened or intimidated another person by word or conduct
To cause physical injury or serious damage to property
Or to cause a public inconvenience
notes: Covers verbal threats, written threats, and threats by conduct. Gang enhancement elevates to felony.

elements: Defendant made a false sworn statement
In an official proceeding
The statement was material
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Perjury in a proceeding that results in conviction of another for a felony is enhanced.

statute_title: Bribery of a Public Servant or Party Officer
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant or party officer
With intent to influence the official action of the public servant
notes: Both the briber and the bribed official can be charged. Receiving a bribe (§ 13-2602(A)(2)) carries the same penalty.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (from detention); Class 3 Felony (from prison, first degree under § 13-2502)
elements: Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody or detention
Defendant was held under authority of law
enhancements: Use of force (§ 13-2502, first degree, Class 3 Felony)
notes: Second degree: escape from custody. First degree (§ 13-2502): escape using physical force, threat, or deadly weapon.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 6 Felony (intentional cruelty, second offense); Class 5 Felony (extreme cruelty)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly subjected an animal to cruel mistreatment or neglect
Or failed to provide adequate food, water, shelter, or veterinary care
notes: Animal fighting (§ 13-2910.01-.04) carries enhanced penalties. Extreme cruelty includes intentional infliction of serious physical injury.

penalty_max: Full sentence on underlying offense may be imposed
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was intentional or without good cause
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose the original sentence, modify conditions, or continue probation. Hearing required. Preponderance of evidence standard.

elements: Defendant was released on community supervision
Defendant violated a condition of supervision
notes: Arizona uses 'community supervision' rather than traditional parole. Board of Executive Clemency makes revocation decisions.

elements: Defendant aided, counseled, agreed to aid, or attempted to aid another person
In planning or committing an offense
With the intent to promote or facilitate the offense
notes: An accomplice is liable to the same extent as the principal. Arizona's accomplice liability is broad — mere encouragement can be sufficient.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense (Class 1 → Class 2, etc.)
penalty_max: Varies — one class below target offense
fine_max: Varies — one class below target offense
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in conduct
That would constitute a crime if the attendant circumstances were as the defendant believed them to be
Or defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission of the offense
notes: Attempt reduces the offense by one class. Attempt to commit a Class 1 Felony is a Class 2 Felony.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies — one class below target offense
fine_max: Varies — one class below target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons
That at least one of them would engage in conduct constituting an offense
With the intent to promote or aid in the commission of the offense
notes: No overt act required for felony conspiracy in Arizona. Renunciation is a defense if the defendant thwarted the success of the conspiracy.
